clue.text: Creature in river representing horse icon

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters of the following words are made to stand for something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A painting of a horse by a river is being described as a sort of icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' signals the anagram: HORSE ICON rearranged gives HINOCEROS, placed after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhino is a large horned African or Asian mammal, a clear example of a creature.

clue.text: Admire efforts to circumvent danger to shipping

indicators.note: to circumvent means to go around, so these words surround the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: Praise attempts to steer around a hazard at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'Admire' and the start of 'efforts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral just below the surface can wreck boats, a classic hazard for sailors.

clue.text: In term son moved closest to the centre

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: During school term a boy changed seats to be nearer the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a link word here: it is the opening piece, and 'moved' signals that the two words after it are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means furthest inward, so nearest the core or middle of something.

clue.text: Hate speaker's stand, lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means the stand is without the letter for power

parts.note: a podium is a platform a speaker stands on
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a lectern that has lost its electricity supply.
explanation.definitionFit: General hatred or strong dislike directed at someone is a noun synonym for hate.

clue.text: People seen outside hotel after each complaint

indicators.note: after means the people-and-hotel piece follows the abbreviation for each

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each, as on price tags

indicators.note: seen outside means the people are placed around the hotel letter

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Guests standing outside a hotel each have a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' means a nation or ethnic group here; 'seen outside' wraps it round the hotel letter and 'after' puts the result behind the abbreviation for each.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a complaint is an ailment, and pain in the ear is one such ailment.

clue.text: Fought against work attitude with Germany

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a pose is an attitude or posture
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A protest against a German stance on employment.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist or contend against something is to have resisted it, matching fought against.

clue.text: Cut yield

definitions.meaning: to trim hair or a hedge short is to cut it
the harvest a field produces in a season

explanation.surface: Two bare words, read as a short instruction about reducing output.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means trim short; the noun means a harvest gathered from farmland.

clue.text: Check covering golf rule

indicators.note: covering means the check word goes around the golf letter

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone verifies a regulation that applies to golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty or the exercise of royal power is rule.

clue.text: Journalists rebel, supporting united force

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the rebel word sits below, holding up the united letter

parts.note: the press are journalists collectively
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: Reporters revolt, backing a united military force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts RISE under U in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone hard to make them act is to compel or force them.

clue.text: European lap dancer's naked beauty

parts.note: a lap or stage of a race or journey is a leg

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer coverings, so only the inner letters of the dancer remain

explanation.surface: A lap dancer from Europe performing nude, admired for her looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips the D and R from DANCER, leaving ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful refinement and style is a kind of beauty, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Occasionally leaving Lennon out in boredom

indicators.note: taking a letter only now and then, leaving out the others, signals every second letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Beatles story where John Lennon leaving the band brings boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally leaving' means take every other letter of LENNON OUT IN, starting from the second: E, N, N, U, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a French borrowing for listless weariness from lack of interest, a synonym.

clue.text: Pure Elvis gyrating? Disgusting!

indicators.note: gyrating means whirling about, so the letters of the two words are spun into a new order; apt for a hip-shaking singer

explanation.surface: A shocked viewer reacting to Elvis Presley's famous hip-swivelling dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something causing strong revulsion; a straight synonym used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Expressions produced by serious experts

parts.note: grim means stern or serious
aces are experts, people who excel at something

explanation.surface: Some faces are being pulled by a panel of solemn specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial expressions of pain or disgust, the twisted faces people pull, are what the answer names.

clue.text: Order egghead to drop one

indicators.note: to drop tells us that the letter for one is let fall from the clever person

parts.note: an egghead is a very clever person, a genius
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction for an intellectual to give up something.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair in a loose sense: in biology a genus is a rank of classification, and 'order' can mean any such class or kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Order here means a kind or class in a classification, which a biological grouping of species is.

clue.text: Sailor's choice crossing river will be preoccupation

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, so the sailor's is AB'S

indicators.note: crossing means the choice word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A sailor picks a route over a river that will occupy all his thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside OPTION, giving ORPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely engrossed in something is total mental engagement, or preoccupation.

clue.text: Sort of cake now cooked and covered in cheese

indicators.note: covered in tells us the cooked letters sit wrapped inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word is prepared and changed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe where a cake is baked and then coated in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal for 'now', and 'covered in' means the cheese is wrapped around the result, not laid on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense, chocolatey square traybake is one kind of cake, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Accident avoided close to girl

parts.note: near means close to
a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A collision was narrowly prevented beside a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape where a collision almost happened is a common idiom for a crash averted.

clue.text: Afraid one forgets to a certain extent, being doomed

indicators.note: to a certain extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone fears a person will forget, believing all is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the end of 'Afraid', takes all of 'one' and the start of 'forgets'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for ruined or beyond saving, matching doomed.

clue.text: Omitted most of team?

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players; leaving out all but one means failing to pick ten of them, and the answer split into three words says just that

explanation.surface: A selector left out nearly all of the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer once it is split as a three-word sentence about ten of an eleven-player side left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary sense, left out or overlooked, matches 'omitted'; the question mark flags the split reading.

clue.text: Unfashionable players in Coventry

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
the cast are the actors in a play

explanation.surface: An out-of-date acting troupe performing in the English city of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them, so 'in Coventry' means shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sent to Coventry is ostracised by the group, which is exactly a rejected person.

clue.text: Dressing, seeing better contact from track and trace

parts.note: to top is to better or beat
during Covid the UK's NHS track and trace app sent a 'ping' alert to contacts of infected people

explanation.surface: A wound dressing improving after a contact-tracing alert during the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'pinged' was British pandemic slang for being told by the NHS app to self-isolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce or garnish put on food, like a salad dressing, is a topping.

clue.text: Soldiers, capturing one, make a mistake getting chains

indicators.note: capturing means the soldiers hold the other pieces within them

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
I is the Roman numeral for one
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Troops seize a prisoner, blunder, and end up in shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chains' looks like fetters but means mountain ranges; 'capturing' sets the other two pieces inside the regiment's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain ranges with jagged peaks, especially in Spain or the Americas, are chains of mountains.

clue.text: Honest and as free at heart

parts.note: since and as both mean because

indicators.note: at heart means only the central letters of the word free are taken

explanation.surface: A truthful person is as unconstrained deep down as they appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and without pretence describes an honest person, a synonym.

clue.text: This may throw light on Boris perhaps accepting endless danger

indicators.note: accepting means the leader's letters take in the shortened danger

parts.note: Boris Johnson was a Prime Minister, PM; 'perhaps' marks him as an example

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for danger is cut off

parts.note: risk means danger

explanation.surface: Something might illuminate a British Prime Minister who keeps taking risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter from the word for danger, and 'accepting' means the Prime Minister's letters take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass block that splits white light into a spectrum throws light in a literal sense.

clue.text: Upset pundit missing Democrat's contribution

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
missing means the letter for Democrat is taken away from the pundit's letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A political commentator is annoyed at a Democrat's absence from the debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from PUNDIT, then 'Upset' rearranges PUNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one puts into a project or discussion is one's contribution to it.

clue.text: Label attached to writer working for military HQ

parts.note: a pen is something one writes with
a tag is a label
on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: A name tag fixed to an author employed at army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided US Department of Defense building in Virginia is the American military headquarters.

clue.text: White must dismiss last couple for record

indicators.note: must dismiss last couple means the final two letters of the egg white word are dropped

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire in white must give out the last pair of batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' is egg white, not a colour; drop its last two letters, EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP or collection of recorded tracks issued together is a record.

clue.text: Errant husband hides like this

indicators.note: hides means the clue words conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A wayward husband conceals himself in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Errant' and the start of 'husband'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this way or so, the same as like this.

clue.text: The setter's voice is calm

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so 'the setter is' gives I'M
in grammar the passive is a voice of the verb, as opposed to active

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler describes their own tone of speech as soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is read as 'the setter is', I'M, not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion, unmoved and composed, is to be calm in manner.

clue.text: Collection at church by bishop

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An offering is taken at a church, next to where the bishop stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of things made or handled together is a set, lot or collection.

clue.text: Crazy sisters with time for nobody, initially

indicators.note: time for nobody means the time letter replaces the other one

parts.note: nuns are religious sisters

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word nobody is used

explanation.surface: Mad nuns who have time for no one at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes N from 'nobody', and T replaces the second N in NUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad or insane, a common informal synonym for crazy.

clue.text: A welcome must include employees with second contracts

indicators.note: must include means the word for welcome has to hold the workers inside it

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men can mean workers or employees, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A greeting to new staff must come with paperwork setting out their terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' places the workers inside the word for welcome; 'employees' as MEN echoes the old phrase 'management and men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally binding deals between parties, such as signed employment terms, are contracts.
